source.author: verg
source.text: non aliter, si parva licet componere magnis, Cecropias innatus apes amor urget habendi, munere quamque suo.
source.text_original: non aliter, si parva licet componere magnis, / Cecropias innatus apes amor urget habendi, / munere quamque suo.
source.text_english: In no other way, if it is permitted to compare small things with great, does an inborn love of possessing drive the Cecropian bees, each with its own gift.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: De Adamantio autem sileo, cujus nomen, si parva licet componere magnis, meo nomine invidiosius est, quod cum in homiliis suis, quas ad vulgum loquitur, communem editionem sequatur: in tomis, id est, in disputatione majori, Hebraica veritate superatus, et suorum circumdatus agminibus, interdum linguae peregrinae quaerit auxilia.
reuse.text_original: De Adamantio autem sileo, cujus nomen, si parva licet componere magnis, meo nomine invidiosius est, quod cum in homiliis suis, quas ad vulgum loquitur, communem editionem sequatur: in tomis, id est, in disputatione majori, Hebraica veritate superatus, et suorum circumdatus agminibus, interdum linguae peregrinae quaerit auxilia.
reuse.text_english: As for Adamantius, I say nothing; for his name, if it is permissible to compare small things with great, is more odious than mine, because, while in his homilies, which he addresses to the common people, he follows the common edition, in his tomes, that is, in the more extended discussion, when overcome by the Hebrew truth and surrounded by his own ranks, he sometimes seeks the help of a foreign tongue.
